name: Sezary Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO-EORTC Diagnostic Criteria for Sezary Syndrome

criteria.description: Generalized erythroderma involving >80% of body surface area
Presence of clonally related malignant T cells (Sezary cells) in peripheral blood
Generalized lymphadenopathy with histopathologic evidence of lymphoma involvement
Aberrant T-cell immunophenotype (e.g., loss of CD7 or CD26) on flow cytometry
Detection of T-cell receptor gene rearrangement confirming clonality

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of erythroderma, circulating Sezary cells, and lymphadenopathy with histopathologic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, hematologic, immunophenotypic, and molecular findings.

pathognomonic.notes: Diffuse redness and scaling of the skin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Circulating Sezary cells in peripheral blood
pathognomonic.notes: Malignant T lymphocytes with cerebriform nuclei
Enlarged lymph nodes due to lymphoma infiltration

common.notes: Hair loss on scalp and eyebrows
Thickening of skin on palms and soles
Changes in nail texture and growth

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing Sezary cells
Flow cytometry demonstrating aberrant T-cell immunophenotype
imaging: PET scan demonstrating metabolically active lymph nodes
genetic: T-cell receptor gene rearrangement confirming clonality
other: Skin biopsy showing epidermotropism of malignant T cells
Lymph node biopsy consistent with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

distinguishingFeatures: Patch and plaque stage skin lesions without significant blood involvement
Absence or low levels of circulating Sezary cells
Slower progression compared to Sezary syndrome
Well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale
History of atopy and allergic conditions
Localized or generalized eczema without malignant cells

redFlags: Presence of circulating malignant T cells
references: Willemze R, Jaffe ES, Burg G, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005;105(10):3768-3785.
Kim YH, Liu HL, Mraz-Gernhard S, et al. Long-term outcome of 525 patients with mycosis fungoides and Sezary syndrome. Arch Dermatol. 2003;139(7):857-866.
Guitart J, Weinstock MA, et al. Sezary syndrome: clinical features and diagnosis. UpToDate. 2024.
